title: Domo Pricing: Is It Worth It In 2026? [Reviewed]
summary: No free tier for new Domo sign-ups, just a 30-day trial. Seats are free, credits are not: AWS lists $3.25 a credit. Worked costs for 25 and 100 users.
body_markdown:
- The 25-user team's 9,245 credits almost exactly fill AWS Marketplace's Tier 1 pool (about 9,230 credits for $30,000). One more daily table pushes it past.
- Refresh frequency moves the bill more than headcount. Refreshing the 25-user team's 20 tables four times a day takes ingestion from 7,300 to 29,200 credits: 31,145 for the year, about $101,000 at $3.25, without a new user.
- Sharing outside the company is priced per account. One external end-customer account is about 1,200 credits a year, about $3,900 at $3.25.
- Users really are free. If all 100 people only read the 25-user team's dashboards, the bill is the 25-user bill. That is the strongest part of Domo's model.
- Both cases sit inside[Vendr](https://www.vendr.com/marketplace/domo) 's observed range, with the 25-user case below the median.


[Source: Vendr.](https://www.vendr.com/marketplace/domo)


Your workload may add Python steps, AI usage or many small tables. Domo publishes the[scoping questions](https://www.domo.com/pricing/guide) its own team uses to size a pool, and its DomoStats reports show where credits go once you are live.


## Why some teams leave Domo over credit pricing (and why others stay)


A Reddit thread titled "Leaving Domo due to Credit Pricing" sits on page one of Google for "domo pricing" (our SERP check, October 27, 2026). I could not open the thread itself, but reviews and vendor write-ups repeat three complaints:


- Renewal shocks.[Coefficient](https://coefficient.io/domo-pricing) reports a verified G2 reviewer whose renewal price rose 1,120% with two months' notice, on the same user count and lower consumption.[BlazeSQL](https://www.blazesql.com/blog/domo-pricing-guide) cites forum reports of renewal offers at 2.5 times the old price. Both come secondhand from vendors that sell alternatives, so treat them as anecdotes, not a rate.
- Forecasting. A credit pool rewards teams that know their refresh schedules and table counts in advance. Teams that add sources on demand find out what a new job costs after it runs.
- Switching cost.[Knowi](https://www.knowi.com/blog/migrating-from-domo/) , another vendor with an alternative to sell, points out that years of Magic ETL dataflows and Beast Mode calculations have to be rebuilt elsewhere, which is why many teams renew anyway.


The other side is real too. One reviewer on[Domo's AWS Marketplace reviews page](https://aws.amazon.com/marketplace/reviews/reviews-list/B077KH5ZZ8?page=5) calls the pricing fair and never feels nickel-and-dimed. Free seats let a company give every manager a dashboard without a license count, which per-seat licensing ([Tableau Viewer seats](https://www.getdot.ai/blog/tableau-pricing) , or Power BI Pro below F64 capacity) does not allow.


My read: credits suit many viewers, a stable set of daily tables and data stored outside Domo. They hurt many small sources refreshed often, external portals, and pipelines added without planning.


Before you sign or renew, get four things in writing: the per-credit rate (AI usage included), whether unused credits roll over, how overage is billed (third-party guides report true-up invoices when you run past your pool), and any cap on renewal increases. Renewals are now negotiated with Progress Software.


## How GetDot prices analysis differently from Domo


GetDot (Dot) is an AI data analyst. It connects to the warehouse or database you already run (such as[BigQuery](https://www.getdot.ai/integrations/bigquery) , Postgres or Snowflake; 45+ sources in all) and answers questions in Slack, Microsoft Teams, email, the web app or any MCP client, with the SQL behind each answer one click away. It queries your warehouse in place, with no data copied or moved, so its credits pay for analysis, not for moving or storing data.


A chat answer costs 1 credit and a longer analysis task about 1 credit per minute. Every plan has unlimited users and is billed on credits, not seats.


- Free: $0, with 300 one-time credits and the full Pro feature set.
- Pro: $180 a month billed annually ($200 month-to-month) with 150 credits a month. Extra credits cost $1.80 on annual billing and $2.00 on monthly billing.
- Team: $720 a month billed annually ($800 month-to-month) with 800 credits a month. Extra credits cost $1.44 on annual billing and $1.60 on monthly billing. Adds workspaces, SSO, row-level security, embedding, a BI migration service and dedicated support.
- Enterprise: custom pricing, with unlimited credits, self-hosted deployment, audit logs, an SLA and a dedicated account manager.


Team's 800 monthly credits cover 800 chat answers, or roughly 800 minutes of analysis, shared by however many people ask. Admins can set weekly credit limits as a flat default, per user, or as shared group pools, and people choose an Economy, Balanced or Frontier model for each question (Energy Mode); our[October 2026 changelog](https://www.getdot.ai/changelog/2026-10-01-fewer-credits) reports Frontier about 40% and Balanced about 30% cheaper in credits than a month earlier. The full price list is on our[pricing page](https://www.getdot.ai/pricing) , with no sales call needed.


### What the credits buy


Answers in the Slack or Teams thread where the question was asked, with a chart when it helps and the query behind it.


Written reviews on a schedule, from current warehouse data, by email or Slack.


Shared definitions: the Context Agent pulls them from dbt, Looker, Tableau, Power BI and your docs, drafts what is missing, and sends every change as a proposal for your team to review.


Evidence, labeled as ours: a configured Dot answered 90% of an assigned 30-task slice of Adyen's DABstep benchmark, against about 52% for Google's Data Science Agent ([how we ran it](https://www.getdot.ai/blog/from-10-to-90-percent-on-adyens-dabstep) ), and Emerge replaced about 50 mismatched dashboards with one source of truth queried from Slack ([case study](https://www.getdot.ai/impact/emerge) ). All LLM providers run with zero data retention, and Dot is SOC 2 Type II ([security overview](https://www.getdot.ai/security) ).


Where Dot falls short of Domo: it does not ingest from hundreds of SaaS sources into its own store, build low-code apps, or host customer portals. Choose Domo when you want ingestion, ETL, dashboards and apps in one bill and you have no warehouse. Choose Dot when your data already lands in a warehouse and the expensive part is answering questions and writing the weekly review. For head-to-head detail see our[Power BI vs Domo](https://www.getdot.ai/blog/microsoft-power-bi-vs-domo) comparison.


You can[start on the free plan](https://app.getdot.ai/register) with 300 credits and the full Pro feature set, no credit card needed, or[book a demo](https://go.getdot.ai/meet) to see it on your own data.
